name: Gingko
family: Ginkgoaceae, the ginkgo family (the only living species)
grown_as: A slow-growing ornamental tree. Garden trees are usually male, grown from cuttings, so bear no fruit. The usual spelling is ginkgo; the library name spells it gingko.
habit: A deciduous tree. Young trees are narrow and gaunt, with a straight leading shoot and a few stiff side branches standing out almost level; 2 to 4 m after many years, eventually 20 m or more. Grey-brown bark, later ridged. Two kinds of shoot: long shoots, and short, stubby, knobbly spur shoots along the older branches.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate and spaced out on long shoots; in tufts of three to five from the tips of the spur shoots
leaf.outline: Fan-shaped, like a maidenhair fern leaflet: 5 to 8 cm across the outer edge and about as long, narrowing to the stalk
leaf.base: A long narrow wedge running into the stalk
leaf.tip: The broad outer edge is wavy and irregularly nicked, usually split by a notch in the middle into two lobes (hence biloba); young trees often have deeper notches
leaf.margin: Smooth along the two straight sides; wavy and nicked only along the outer edge
leaf.veins: No midrib: many fine veins fan out from the base, forking again and again, running parallel to the outer edge
leaf.surface: Smooth, hairless, leathery, the same on both sides
leaf.colour: Fresh light green; clear butter yellow in autumn, all falling within a few days

fruit: Female trees only (rare in gardens): plum-like seeds 2 to 3 cm, yellow-orange with a waxy bloom, hanging in pairs on long stalks from the spurs; the flesh smells foul when it falls. Not drawn.
seedling: Not drawn: grown as a bought tree
winter: Bare tree. Stiff, level branches studded with short, knobbly spur shoots, each ending in a small dome-shaped brown bud and ringed by old leaf scars.

leaf: fan-shaped leaf on a long stalk
many fine forking veins fanning from the base, no midrib
wavy outer edge with a central notch making two lobes
young: a narrow, gaunt young tree with a straight leader and a few stiff level branches
dormant: short knobbly spur shoots studding the branches, each with a small dome bud
growing: fan-shaped leaves in tufts on the spurs along the branches
autumn: the same fan-shaped leaves in tufts
a few fallen yellow fans on the ground

look_alikes: Nothing else has fan-shaped leaves with forking parallel veins. Maidenhair fern leaflets are similar in shape but tiny and on black wiry stalks.
